title: Seaming amigurumi pieces
subtitle: Attaching safety eyes, stuffing and closing the body, and joining separate limbs invisibly
excerpt: Amigurumi assembly means attaching eyes, stuffing the piece firmly, closing the opening, and sewing on limbs in the correct positions. The finishing order matters. Eyes must go in before the piece is stuffed and closed; limbs go on last.
sourceNotes: Edie Eckman, The Crochet Answer Book (Storey Publishing). Contemporary amigurumi design references.

glossaryTerms.definition: A plastic eye with a serrated shank and a backing washer that locks into place when pushed through crochet fabric. The washer cannot be removed without cutting the eye apart, making it secure for soft toys.
An invisible seaming stitch worked from the outside of a piece, alternating small horizontal stitches on each side of the seam. When pulled taut, the stitches disappear inside the fabric.
The final round of a decreasing amigurumi piece. Typically worked as six to eight stitches, then the yarn is drawn through all remaining stitches to pull them closed.

content.text: Amigurumi assembly follows a fixed order: eyes before stuffing, stuffing before closing, limbs after the body is closed. Each step depends on the previous one being complete. Insert
safety eyes
first, while you can still reach inside to lock the washer in place. Stuff firmly, then close the opening. Attach limbs by sewing through both the limb and the body to position them correctly.
What you need

items.name: Safety eyes
items.note: 6 mm to 9 mm for most amigurumi; 12 mm for larger pieces. Never use for toys intended for children under 3; embroider eyes instead.

items.name: Polyester fibrefill stuffing
items.note: Stuff firmly rather than lightly. Under-stuffed amigurumi goes soft and loses its shape.

items.name: Matching yarn for seaming
items.note: Use the same yarn as the piece, or a finer strand in the same colour if the body yarn is too thick

items.name: Pins or stitch markers
items.note: For positioning limbs on the body before sewing

content.text: Step 1: inserting safety eyes
Identify the eye placement on the head before stuffing. Count the stitches and rows to ensure the eyes are symmetric. Use pins to mark the position.

Push the shank of the safety eye through the fabric from the outside. Reach inside the piece and press the backing washer firmly down the shank until it clicks into the groove at the base of the shank.
Test the eye by pulling it firmly from the outside. It should not move. The washer cannot be removed without tools once it is locked.
Step 2: stuffing and closing
Fill the piece firmly with fibrefill. Push stuffing into any tight corners or appendages with a pencil or blunt stick.
For the
closing round
: thread the yarn tail onto the tapestry needle. Run the needle through the front loop only of each remaining stitch, going around the full circle.
Pull the yarn tail firmly to gather the remaining stitches closed. Pass the needle through the centre of the gather once more to secure it, then weave the tail into the body of the piece.
Step 3: attaching limbs with ladder stitch
Pin the limb to the body in the correct position. Check symmetry by holding the piece at arm's length and viewing it from the front.

Thread the tapestry needle with matching yarn. Bring the needle up through the body at one edge of where the limb will sit. Work a small horizontal stitch through the edge of the limb at the same height.
Bring the needle back through the body directly opposite. Work the next horizontal stitch through the limb. Pull the thread gently taut after every two stitches. This is
ladder stitch
: the horizontal stitches pull inside the seam as you tighten, making the join invisible.
Continue around the full edge of the limb attachment point. Pull firmly to close and knot off inside the body.
Common problems

items.symptom: The eyes are not level or the placement looks wrong after locking
items.cause: The backing washer was locked before the position was confirmed, or the eyes were inserted without checking from the front.
items.fix: Once locked, a safety eye cannot be repositioned without breaking it. Use embroider marker on a swatch to test eye placement before inserting the final eyes.

items.symptom: The limb sags or droops after attachment
items.cause: The seam thread was too fine for the weight of the limb, or the closing gather was not tight enough.
items.fix: Reinforce the attachment by passing the needle through the join point several more times. Use a doubled strand of yarn for heavier limbs.

items.symptom: The closing gap is visible after pulling the yarn through
items.cause: The gather was pulled only once rather than twice, or the yarn was cut too short before the second securing pass.
items.fix: Pass the needle through the gather a second time and pull firmly before cutting. The closing stitch needs to be anchored in two directions to hold.

content.text: What to try next

A simple sphere with two arms makes the best first seaming practice. There are only three pieces to join. The scale is large enough to see the stitches clearly, and the round shape is forgiving if the seam is slightly off.
